messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: streaming-proxy-high-latency (p95/p99 breach) — streaming-tail-sockets. Detected at 2026-03-15T02:12:25Z. p95=480ms (SLO 200ms), p99=1.8s (SLO 500ms). Affected routes: /v1/stream, websocket gateway. Errors: increased ALB 504s and client disconnects. Link: https://infra.metrics/reports/streaming-proxy
maya: I'm on it. Pulling traces now. seeing concentrated tail on one AZ (eu-west-1b). :mag_right:
samir: Repro from curl shows streaming SSE stalls at ~300ms chunk gaps then big pause:
```
$ curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream
data: {"token":"a..."}
\n
# ~320ms
\n
# silence ~1.5s
\n
# then chunks resume
```
maya: Looks like the ALB is returning `HTTP 504` for some connections when chunk gaps exceed 1s. ALB idle timeout config is 60s though — but we have a downstream keepalive/tcp-proxy setting that resets connections earlier on slow clients.
li: Taking lead. Oncall SRE here. First step: confirm proxy pool and connection queue lengths.
alice-eng: Logs show `proxy_write_blocked` spikes coincident with p99. Agent logs excerpt:
```
proxy-1 | 02:11:48.123 write_blocked for client_id=svc-123 queue_len=134
proxy-1 | 02:11:48.456 backpressure=high
```
bob-platform: Rolling window shows one proxy host with 88% CPU and 90% socket backlog. Might be a hot shard. I'll drain and shift traffic.
cs-andy: Heads-up: production customer "BrightCall" reported timeouts in their streaming integration at ~02:10 UTC, customers on EU region mostly. They've opened a ticket referencing session drops.
samir: Quick mitigation options we can do live:
- scale proxy pool by +3 instances in eu-west-1b
- reduce per-connection write buffer size (to force smaller bursts)
- temporarily relax ALB idle/keepalive mismatch by toggling proxy keepalive to true
maya: I can trigger a scale now. Will also add a coarse rate-limit on long-lived streams to prevent clients spamming reopens.
li: Do the scale and buffer tweak. I'll apply a proxy config change to increase `socket_write_timeout` from 800ms -> 1500ms for EU region to avoid premature timeouts. Command I'm running:
```
# scale replicas
kubectl -n infra scale deployment streaming-proxy --replicas=8 --selector=region=eu-west-1b
# patch configmap
kubectl -n infra patch cm proxy-config --patch '{"data":{"socket_write_timeout":"1500"}}'
```
bob-platform: Draining proxy-5 now, shifting ~18% traffic to proxy-6/7. CPU normalizing on proxy-6.
maya: After scale and patch, p95 dropped to 210ms, p99 to 520ms — still slightly over p99 SLO but much improved. No new 504s in last 2m.
cs-andy: BrightCall says streams are back but intermittent replays happened. They want a postmortem and ETA on fix.
li: Good. Next steps: 1) keep scaled pool for 60 minutes 2) run canary with connection pacing patch to ensure we don't regress 3) dig into root cause: why backup in single AZ. Assigning to samir + alice-eng for deep dive.
samir: Early hypothesis: client backpressure + proxy write buffer scheduling leads to socket starvation on one host. We saw a burst of long-lived streams from a single customer that skewed the connection distribution. Will check load balancer stickiness and upstream routing.
alice-eng: Also fetching kernel socket metrics (tcp_wmem, tcp_rmem) and ulimit counts. If one host hit ephemeral port exhaustion it would explain stalls.
maya: For visibility, added alert to detect per-host socket_backlog > 100 for 2m. Also created temporary Grafana panel tile for `proxy_write_blocked` per host.
li: Customer comms — cs-andy please tell BrightCall: we mitigated the surge, we're keeping capacity boosted and investigating root cause; will follow up within 6 hours with postmortem.
cs-andy: On it. Message drafted and sent.
bob-platform: Monitoring: p99 trending back down to 420ms, no new 504s. I'll leave traffic redistributed and keep an eye on cpu/sockets.
maya: Any objections to making `socket_write_timeout=1500ms` the default for EU for next 24h? It's safe and buys us headroom.
li: Fine as temporary. We'll revert after root cause confirmed.
samir: Logging more detailed client IDs from proxy to see if a single customer caused skew. Dumping top talkers now.
alice-eng: Found that a batch job from BrightCall's integration opened 400 concurrent long-poll streams in a 30s window — this matches the timing.
li: That's the smoking gun. Action items:
- samir: collect full traces + correlation IDs (priority)
- alice-eng: verify LB stickiness config + haproxy rules
- bob-platform: run capacity test for worst-case 500 simultaneous long-poll streams
- maya: keep scaled pool live and alert on regressions
- cs-andy: coordinate customer comms and timeline
cs-andy: Customer asked for mitigation steps on their side — recommend connection ramping and exponential backoff. Sending guidance.
maya: Will open incident ticket for postmortem. Tags: streaming, proxy, customer-impact, p99
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-0671. Owner: li. Severity: Sev2. Timeline link: https://incidents.company/INC-20260315-0671
li: Marking this thread as handoff-complete for oncall. Taking it to postmortem and follow-ups. If p99 creeps back up I'll re-pager.
maya: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
